all_up_to_date:
✅ *Verificación de Docker*
Todas las imágenes están actualizadas.
container_not_in_list: ⚠️ Contenedor `{name}` no está en la lista.
rate_limit: Límite alcanzado. Ejecute `docker login` en el host y monte las credenciales.
help_detail_checkimages:
*/checkimages* — dry-run for /cleanup.

Shows how much disk space would be reclaimed by running `/cleanup` right now (unused images + build cache), read from `docker system df`. Also flags whether auto-cleanup on the disk warning is currently ON or OFF.
checkimages_none: 🧹 Nothing to clean up right now — no unused images or build cache.
checkimages_auto_off: 💡 Auto-cleanup on disk warning: OFF — set `DISK_WARN_AUTO_CLEANUP=true` (or enable it in Web UI → Settings) to reclaim automatically.
cleanup_none: ✅ No se encontraron imágenes sin usar.
selfupdate_queued: ⏳ Container updates in progress — self-update queued, it will start automatically once they finish.
selfupdate_dequeued: 🚀 Container updates finished — starting the queued self-update...
selfupdate_queue_cancelled: ⚠️ Queued self-update cancelled — the update run hit an unexpected error. Run /selfupdate again when ready.
cleanup_busy: ⏳ Updates in progress — cleanup skipped so it can't delete a freshly pulled image. Try again once they finish.
monitor_oom: 🧠 {name} was OOM-killed (exit code {code}) — it ran out of memory. Consider raising its memory limit.
monitor_crash_restart: 🔁 {name} se bloqueó (salida {code}) y su política de reinicio lo reinició a las {when} (reinicio #{count}).
monitor_mass_stop: ⚠️ {name}: {count} de {total} contenedores se detuvieron a la vez (host apagado o reiniciado).
monitor_mass_host_down: ⚠️ {host} parece haberse apagado o reiniciado — {count} de {total} contenedores se detuvieron a la vez.
monitor_mass_cluster: ⚠️ {count} contenedores en {host} se detuvieron a la vez.
monitor_mass_footer: Las alertas de fallo por contenedor se agruparon en esta. El registro de cada contenedor está adjunto; el historial completo está en el registro de eventos.
monitor_mass_file_caption: Registros de los contenedores de {host}, capturados al detenerse.
web_events_empty_hint: Health flips, non-zero exits, OOM kills and crash-restarts will show up here.
monitor_top_cpu: CPU más alta en el momento del evento: {list}
events_empty: 🩺 No container events recorded yet. Health flips, non-zero exits, OOM kills and crash-restarts will show up here.
help_events: Recent container events (crashes, OOM, health flips)
help_detail_events: Shows the most recent monitor events from the persistent event log — health changes, exits with non-zero codes, OOM kills and crash-restarts. Same data as the Web UI's Container Events section. Events are recorded by the state monitor (MONITOR=true, default on).
lifecycle_busy: ⏳ Updates in progress — {action} refused so it can't interfere with a running update. Try again once they finish.
selfupdate_restarting: Iniciando auto-actualización... El bot estará brevemente fuera de línea.
selfupdate_failed_id: ❌ Auto-actualización fallida: ID de contenedor no encontrado.
manual_message: 👍 Las actualizaciones no se realizarán automáticamente.
pin_added: 📌 `{name}` fijado — se omitirá en las actualizaciones.
unpin_removed: 📌 `{name}` desfijado — se incluirá en las actualizaciones.
selfupdate_recreate_failed:
⚠️ Self-update failed: the new container couldn't be created and Docksentry rolled back to the previous version (still running). Helper output:
```
{detail}
```
check_scoped_uptodate: ✅ {count} container(s) matching `{pattern}` are up to date.
update_scoped_none: ✅ No pending updates among containers matching `{pattern}`.
update_usage: Usage: `/update <name>` or `/update <glob>` (e.g. `/update gluetun-*`). Updates only matching containers that have a pending update.
help_detail_update:
*/update* — Update containers by name or glob

`/update <name>` — check + update one container (if it has an update).
`/update <glob>` — update every matching container that has a pending update, e.g. `/update gluetun-*`.

📌 Runs a check first, then applies only matching containers with updates — same path as the Update-all button (group order, dependents cascade, health-check + rollback). Typing the pattern is the go-ahead, so no extra confirm. Use `/check <glob>` first to preview.
lifecycle_refused_protected: 🛡 `{name}` is protected from Stop. Remove the protection first (container detail page in the Web UI, or `/protect {name}`). Restart still works.
web_detail_protect_hint: Hide and refuse the Stop action for this container, so you can't accidentally take down something you depend on (e.g. the VPN/tunnel carrying your remote access). Restart and updates still work.
help_protect: /protect — Protect a container from being stopped
help_detail_protect:
*/protect* — Protect a container from Stop

`/protect` — list protected containers.
`/protect <name>` — toggle stop-protection for a container.

📌 A protected container has no Stop button (Telegram + Web UI) and Stop is refused — so you can't accidentally take down something you depend on, like the VPN/tunnel carrying your remote access. Restart and updates still work. Also settable on the container detail page in the Web UI.
protect_empty: No stop-protected containers. `/protect <name>` to add one.
protect_on: 🛡 `{name}` is now protected from Stop. Restart still works.
protect_off: `{name}` is no longer protected from Stop.
web_sort_name: Sort by name (click to cycle A→Z, Z→A, group order)
changelog_current:
📄 *You're on the latest — v{version}* ({date})
What this version brought:
cooldown_empty: No per-container update cooldowns set. `/cooldown <name> <seconds>` to add one.
cooldown_bad_value: ⚠️ Seconds must be a number (0–600). E.g. `/cooldown llama-server 20`.
cooldown_set: ✅ `{name}` update cooldown set to *{seconds}s* — Docksentry will pause that long after recreating it before the next container.
help_detail_cooldown:
*/cooldown* — Per-container update cooldown

`/cooldown` — list containers with a cooldown set.
`/cooldown <name> <seconds>` — after recreating this container in a batch update, Docksentry waits this long before recreating the next one (0–600s; 0 clears).
`/cooldown <name>` — show the current value.

📌 For heavy containers (GPU/large RAM) whose load peak would otherwise overlap the next recreate and exhaust memory. Opt-in, default 0. Also settable on the container detail page in the Web UI.
web_detail_cooldown_hint: After recreating this container in a batch update, wait this many seconds before the next one. For heavy GPU/RAM containers whose startup peak would otherwise overlap the next recreate and run out of memory. 0 = off.
selfupdate_retag: 🔁 *Re-joining the rolling line* — the image bits are identical, but I'll recreate so your container tracks `{new}` instead of `{old}` from now on. Bot will be briefly offline.
groups_none: No container groups configured yet. Create one in the Web UI → Groups.
groups_not_found: ⚠️ No group matching `{name}`. Try /groups to list them.
group_detail_rd_on: 🔁 restart-dependents: *on* — updating the head restarts the others
help_detail_groups:
*/groups* — Container Groups

`/groups` — list all groups with member count and the 👑 head.
`/groups <name>` — one group's members (🟢 running / ⚪ stopped), its restart-dependents setting, and — for a `restart_dependents` group — a button to restart the dependents now (waits for the head to be healthy first).

📌 Read-only except the restart button. Create / edit groups in the Web UI → Groups.
dryrun_title:
🧪 *Dry run — what an update would do*
_Nothing is changed below._
dryrun_major: ⚠ major jump `{old}` → `{new}` — would ask to confirm first
dryrun_footer: _Nothing was changed. Run /check and tap Update to apply._
web_detail_trust_hint: After an update, accept this container as healthy when it is running — even if its healthcheck reports unhealthy. For containers with brittle healthchecks (e.g. VPN-sidecar dependents whose probe hits the wrong namespace). A crash-loop or a container that isn't running still counts as a failed update.
startup_reason_signal: ↻ _El reinicio se produjo tras una señal de parada externa ({signal}) — p. ej. un reinicio del host, `docker restart`, o el reinicio del demonio de Docker. Docksentry no se reinició solo._
web_topic_id_placeholder: Opcional — para grupos con temas activados
web_auto_cleanup_hint: Tras cada actualización automática exitosa, elimina imágenes sin usar de más de 24h.
web_cleanup_grace_hours_hint: Solo eliminar imágenes sin usar desde al menos este tiempo. Más alto = más seguro.
web_cleanup_backup_days_hint: Cuánto tiempo conservar los tarballs de respaldo.
web_cleanup_backup_local_only_hint: Guarda las imágenes construidas localmente (sin digest de registro) como tarball antes de eliminarlas.
web_disk_warn_percent_hint: Notify when disk usage exceeds this percent (one warning per day max).
web_disk_warn_auto_cleanup_hint: Run cleanup automatically when the warning threshold is crossed.
web_quiet_hours_hint: Auto-notifications during this window are dropped (manual command replies always go through). Leave both empty to disable.
web_windows_intro: Restrict auto-updates to specific time-of-day and weekday windows. Containers without a window entry update without restriction.
web_windows_days_hint: Leave all unchecked to allow every weekday.
web_major_pending_intro: These containers have a pending major-version bump. Major updates can break configs — confirm or skip.
web_settings_intro: Configure how Docksentry checks for, applies, and notifies about updates. Changes here override the corresponding environment variables and persist across restarts.
web_cron_help: 5-field cron expression (minute hour day month weekday). Default 0 18 * * * = daily at 18:00.
web_excluded_help: Comma-separated list of container names to skip during checks (e.g. 'plex,nextcloud'). Useful for containers you only want to update manually.
web_debug_help: Send detailed update-check logs to Telegram on every run. Useful for diagnosing why a container is or isn't being seen.
web_auto_selfupdate_help: When on, Docksentry pulls and applies its own image update on every scheduled cron tick. Off = self-update only on demand via /selfupdate or the maintenance button.
web_updates_tab_hint: Per-container auto-update flags, pin/unpin, and the major-confirm toggle live on the Status page — pick which containers get treated which way there.
web_topic_id_help: Optional. Set this to send Telegram messages to a specific topic/thread inside a forum-style group, instead of the general topic.
web_discord_help: Optional. Set to a Discord channel webhook URL to mirror updates as rich embeds in Discord. Find it under: Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks.
web_webhook_help: Optional. Generic JSON POST endpoint — works with Ntfy, Gotify, Home Assistant, n8n, etc. Receives all events as JSON payloads.
web_maintenance_intro: Manual one-shot actions. Each runs in the background and reports the result via the configured notification channels.
web_maintenance_explain: Image Cleanup removes unused Docker images older than {grace}h. With Backup local-only enabled, locally-built images are saved as tarballs in {dir} and kept for {days} days. Self-Update pulls the latest Docksentry image and recreates this container.
web_confirm_cleanup: Run docker image prune now? Unused images older than the grace period will be deleted.
web_confirm_selfupdate: Self-update Docksentry? The container will pull the latest image and restart itself — this Web UI will be briefly unavailable.
web_info_credentials_hint: Bot Token and Chat ID can only be set via environment variables. WEB_PORT and WEB_PASSWORD are also env-only — changing them in a UI you're using right now would lock you out.
web_badge_update_tt: An update is available — open the row's update button or use Bulk Update.
web_badge_auto_tt: Auto-update enabled — runs on the next scheduled tick.
web_label_authoritative: Controlled by a docksentry.* label in the compose file — remove the label there to change this.
web_monitor_only_tt: Solo observar: Docksentry vigila este contenedor e informa de actualizaciones, pero nunca lo actualiza.
web_env_override_tt: El entorno define {var}={value}, pero gana el valor guardado aquí. Cambia este campo y guarda para sobrescribirlo, o elimina la clave de settings.json para volver a seguir el entorno.
web_env_override_secret_tt: El entorno define {var}, pero gana el valor guardado aquí. Cambia este campo y guarda para sobrescribirlo, o elimina la clave de settings.json para volver a seguir el entorno.
web_badge_major_tt: Major-update confirmation enabled — major version bumps require manual confirm.
web_bulk_pin_tt: Pin all selected — they'll be skipped on update checks.
web_container_detail_hint: This page will host per-container history, logs, and per-container update settings (window, major-confirm, auto-update). For now use the Status page actions.
web_history_empty_hint: Updates will be recorded here once they happen.
web_container_not_found_hint: It may have been removed or renamed. Return to the status page.
web_detail_auto_hint: When on, this container is updated automatically on every scheduled tick (subject to grace + window).
web_detail_major_hint: When on, SemVer major bumps for this container require manual confirmation.
web_detail_pin_hint: Pinned containers are skipped on update checks entirely.
web_detail_window_intro: Restrict auto-update to a specific time-of-day and weekdays. Empty = no restriction.
web_container_history_empty: No update history for this container yet.
web_container_history_empty_hint: Updates for this container will be recorded here.
web_weekly_hint: Sends a once-a-week digest of updates, failures, rollbacks, and disk usage to all configured channels.
web_groups_intro: Group containers that should update in a specific order. Auto-updates respect the listed order, with an optional wait between containers (e.g. database first, then app). On failure, remaining containers in the group are skipped.
web_groups_empty_hint: Add a group below to coordinate updates across multiple containers.
web_groups_containers_label: Containers (Ctrl/Cmd-click to select multiple, in update order)
web_groups_containers_hint: Order matters: the first container in the list is updated first. Use ↑/↓ buttons after creation to reorder.
web_groups_delete_confirm: Delete group "{name}"? Containers in the group will become unassigned.
web_setup_intro: Let's get you set up in four quick steps. You can change everything later under Settings.
web_setup_lang_intro: All notifications and the Web UI will use this language.
web_setup_schedule_title: When should Docksentry check for updates?
web_setup_schedule_intro: Pick a preset or type a custom cron expression below.
web_setup_cron_help: Format: minute hour day month weekday. Example: 0 18 * * * = daily at 18:00.
web_setup_channels_intro: Notifications go out across all configured channels in parallel. The Web UI alone is also fine.
web_setup_telegram_on: Telegram is configured via environment variables. Inline buttons + commands work out of the box.
web_setup_telegram_off: Telegram needs BOT_TOKEN and CHAT_ID environment variables. You can run headless without it — Web UI + Discord/Webhook is enough.
web_setup_auto_intro: You can change this per container later. This is just the default.
web_setup_auto_manual: Notify only — I decide each time
web_setup_auto_manual_hint: Updates are detected and you get a message with buttons. Nothing happens until you click.
web_setup_auto_all_hint: Every container with an available update is updated automatically on the configured schedule. Health-check + auto-rollback protect against bad updates.
web_setup_auto_picky: Auto-update only what I pick later
web_setup_auto_picky_hint: I'll go to Status and toggle auto-update per container individually after the wizard.
web_setup_skip: Skip — I know what I'm doing
web_maint_mode_intro: Pause scheduled checks and notifications during host maintenance. Manual updates still work.
web_maint_status_inactive: Maintenance mode is off — scheduled checks run as normal.
maintenance_usage: Usage: `/maintenance` to see status, `/maintenance 2h` (or `30m`, `1d`, `forever`) to enable, `/maintenance off` to disable.
maintenance_enabled_forever: 🛠 Maintenance mode enabled — until manually disabled.
web_note_intro: Free-text memo for this container, visible in the status table tooltip.
web_note_placeholder: e.g. "runs on host network — careful with port changes"
selfupdate_restarting_then_check: Starting self-update — your container update check will resume right after restart.
selfupdate_resumed_check: ✅ Restarted on v{version} — checking your containers...
web_allowed_users_help: Optional — comma-separated list of Telegram user IDs allowed to control the bot. Useful in groups where you don't want every member to trigger updates. Leave empty to allow anyone in the configured chat.
web_groups_restart_dependents: Restart dependents when the head container updates
web_groups_restart_dependents_hint: When the FIRST container in the list (the "head", e.g. Gluetun) gets updated, all other group members are restarted after the head reports healthy. Use for VPN-sidecar / shared-network-namespace setups where dependents lose connectivity when the namespace owner restarts.
web_bot_label_help: Optional prefix prepended to every notification — useful when multiple Docksentry instances post into the same Telegram group, Discord channel, or webhook so you can tell which host a message is from. Max 32 chars.
help_changelog: /changelog — Show what's new in versions ahead of yours
docksentry_update_hint: 🚀 *Docksentry update available* — run /selfupdate to apply, or /changelog to preview what's new.
changelog_up_to_date: ✅ You're on *v{version}* — no newer versions in the changelog.
migration_self_autoupdate_removed: 🛡 *Heads up:* this Docksentry container was on its own auto-update list. Auto-updating ourselves through the regular flow killed the process before recreate could happen (see #16). Removed from the list. Use `/selfupdate` (manual) or `AUTO_SELFUPDATE=true` (env) for self-updates instead.
help_lifecycle: /start /stop /restart <name> — Lifecycle control for a single container
lifecycle_usage: Usage: `/start <name>`, `/stop <name>`, or `/restart <name>`. Partial name matching works the same as `/pin`.
lifecycle_refused_self: 🛡 Refused to {action} `{name}` — that's me. Use /selfupdate for self-updates.
web_lifecycle_confirm_stop: Stop {name}? The container will go offline until it's started again.
selfupdate_invalid_version: ❌ `{version}` doesn't look like a semver tag (`X.Y.Z`). Examples: `/selfupdate 1.17.4`, `/selfupdate previous`.
selfupdate_previous_fetch_failed: ❌ Couldn't fetch the changelog to resolve `previous`: {error}
selfupdate_previous_none: ❌ No version older than v{current} found in the changelog.
help_autocomplete_hint: 💡 *Tip:* type `/` in this chat — Telegram shows an autocomplete picker with all commands and their descriptions.
changelog_container_source:
📄 *Changelog for* `{name}`

Docksentry doesn't fetch and parse arbitrary container changelogs — projects use too many different formats (Keep-a-Changelog, GitHub Releases, HISTORY.md, none at all) for a reliable summary. Instead, here's the upstream source:

🔗 {url}

Releases are typically at `/releases` and changelog files at `/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md`.
changelog_container_url_only:
📄 *Changelog for* `{name}`

This image only sets the `image.url` label (product page, not source repo), so I can't link you directly at the changelog. Try:

🔗 {url}

Look for a 'Changelog', 'Release notes', or 'What's new' section.
changelog_container_none:
📄 *Changelog for* `{name}`

No source label and the image reference doesn't map to a known registry. Check the image's documentation or `docker inspect {name}` for hints.
web_link_intro: URL opcional para este contenedor: repositorio de origen, página de releases o changelog upstream. Envuelve el nombre del contenedor en las notificaciones de actualización y aparece como 🔗 junto al contenedor en la Web UI. Anula la detección automática de las etiquetas OCI; déjalo vacío para volver a ella. Una etiqueta docksentry.link en el archivo compose tiene prioridad sobre este campo.
help_setlink: /setlink <name> <url> — Set the changelog / repo link shown in /changelog and update notifications. Omit URL to clear.
setlink_usage: Usage: `/setlink container_name https://github.com/...` — or `/setlink container_name` to clear.
setlink_cleared: 🔗 `{name}` link cleared — OCI labels will be used again.
help_per_command_hint: 💬 *Per-command help:* `/help <command>` shows parameters, examples and side effects for one command, e.g. `/help cleanup`.
help_detail_status:
*/status* — Container overview

`/status` — list of all containers (running + stopped) with health icons, uptime and image.
`/status <name>` — full detail for one container: state, health, ports, volumes, restart policy, plus inline action buttons (Update / Restart / Stop).

📌 Partial name matches work: `/status jelly` resolves to `jellyfin` if unambiguous.
help_detail_check:
*/check* — Trigger an update check now

Forces an immediate scan instead of waiting for the next `CRON_SCHEDULE` tick. Compares the local image digest of every running container against the registry. Pending updates land in a new "🔄 Updates Available" notification with one-tap buttons.

⚠️ Refuses while an update is already running (race-lock since v1.18.9).
help_detail_updates:
*/updates* — Show pending updates

Lists every container Docksentry has previously flagged as having an update available, with action buttons. Equivalent to re-displaying the last "Updates Available" notification without re-running the check.

📌 Empty when nothing is pending.
help_detail_cleanup:
*/cleanup* — Remove unused Docker images

Removes images older than `CLEANUP_GRACE_HOURS` (default 24h) that no running container references. Set `CLEANUP_BACKUP_LOCAL_ONLY=true` to back locally-built images up as tarballs first (in `/data/backups/`).

⚠️ Side effects: posts a notification, frees disk. Check before / after with `/status`.
help_detail_lifecycle:
*/start /stop /restart* — Single-container lifecycle

`/start <name>` — start a stopped container
`/stop <name>` — stop a running container (refuses on self for safety)
`/restart <name>` — stop + start in one shot

Partial name matches work. Stop refuses on the Docksentry container itself.
help_detail_maintenance:
*/maintenance* — Pause scheduled checks

`/maintenance <duration>` — silence auto-updates for the duration (e.g. `2h`, `30m`, `1d`, `forever`).
`/maintenance off` — re-enable immediately.
`/maintenance` (no arg) — show current state.

📌 Manual `/check` and `/update` still work during maintenance. Only the cron-driven auto-update is paused.
help_detail_history:
*/history* — Recent update history

Last 20 update events (success + failure) with date arrows, image size deltas and version arrows when the upstream image carries an `org.opencontainers.image.version` label. Includes self-updates of Docksentry itself since v1.17.6.
help_detail_pin:
*/pin /unpin* — Skip / re-enable updates for a container

`/pin <name>` — exclude from update checks (won't appear in `/updates`)
`/unpin <name>` — re-include
`/pin` (no arg) — list pinned

📌 Useful when you want to stay on a specific image version without env-var pinning.
help_detail_autoupdate:
*/autoupdate* — Toggle silent auto-update for a container

`/autoupdate <name>` — flip auto-update on / off for that container
`/autoupdate` (no arg) — list containers with auto-update enabled

📌 Auto-updated containers don't generate a "Updates Available" prompt — they run on the next cron tick with no button-tap needed. Use carefully: combine with `restart_dependents` Container Groups when a container has sidecars.
help_detail_setlink:
*/setlink* — Definir el enlace de repositorio / changelog de un contenedor

`/setlink <nombre> <url>` — guardar un enlace (debe ser una URL `http://` o `https://` completa; cualquier otra cosa se rechaza)
`/setlink <nombre>` (sin url) — borrarlo y volver a las etiquetas

📌 Una etiqueta de contenedor `docksentry.link` tiene prioridad sobre este comando: ponla en tu archivo compose y el enlace viaja con el contenedor.
📌 El enlace alimenta la salida de `/changelog`, el enlace al repositorio en las notificaciones de actualización Y el icono 🔗 de la Web UI. Útil cuando la imagen upstream no define la etiqueta OCI `org.opencontainers.image.source`.
help_detail_audit:
*/audit* — Inspect-coverage audit for a container

`/audit <name>` — run the v1.19.0 audit logger against this container's `docker inspect` and report any HostConfig / Config fields that are non-default but NOT restored on recreate.

📌 If the output is empty, you're safe — every important field is preserved. If anything shows up, please file an issue with the lines so we can extend coverage.
help_detail_selfupdate:
*/selfupdate* — Update Docksentry itself

`/selfupdate` — pull `:latest` and recreate (helper-container swap)
`/selfupdate <X.Y.Z>` — pin to a specific version (e.g. `/selfupdate 1.19.0`)
`/selfupdate previous` — roll back to the last released version older than the running one

📌 Different code path than container updates — `selfupdate` uses a helper container to swap PID 1.
help_detail_changelog:
*/changelog* — What's new

`/changelog` — list Docksentry releases newer than the running version, with links
`/changelog <name>` — show the repo / changelog link for one container

📌 We don't try to fetch and parse arbitrary container changelogs (formats vary too much) — for containers we point you at the upstream source repo.
help_detail_debug:
*/debug* — Toggle debug logging

`/debug` — flip debug on / off. When on, internal events (cron ticks, network attach, audit-mode warnings, container resolve hits) appear in `docker logs docksentry`.

📌 No impact on Telegram chat output — only on host-side logs.
help_detail_logs:
*/logs* — Show recent container logs

`/logs <name>` — last 30 log lines from the container, formatted as a code block.

📌 Useful right after an update report: `❌ jellyfin: …rolled back` → then `/logs jellyfin` to see what crashed.
help_detail_lang:
*/lang* — Switch the bot language

`/lang en` or `/lang de` — change to English or German. Other 14 languages fall back to English strings (translation contributions welcome).
`/lang` (no arg) — show current language.
help_detail_settings:
*/settings* — Current configuration

Shows the active schedule, language, auto-selfupdate flag, healthcheck max-starting wait, debug state and other env-driven settings. Read-only via Telegram; the Web UI lets you edit most of these without restart.
help_detail_help:
*/help* — Command reference

`/help` — list of all commands with a one-line summary
`/help <command>` — detailed help for a specific command (synopsis, parameters, examples)

📌 The autocomplete picker (type `/` in this chat) is faster for discovery — try it.
audit_usage: Usage: `/audit container_name` — checks the container's inspect for fields we don't restore on recreate.
audit_clean: ✅ `{name}`: clean — every non-default HostConfig and Config field is restored on recreate.
audit_findings_header:
🔍 *Audit for* `{name}`:

The following fields are non-default in your inspect but NOT restored by `_build_run_args`. On recreate they'd be silently dropped.
audit_footer: 📬 Please [open an issue](https://github.com/amayer1983/docksentry/issues) with this list so we can extend coverage.
web_groups_page_intro: Manage VPN-sidecar / shared-namespace stacks here. The first container in a group is the *head* — when it's updated, dependents are restarted (if you enable `restart_dependents`). Drag rows to reorder.
web_groups_head_tt: The head container — when it's updated, the rest of the group reacts (restart, recreate, etc).
web_groups_stale_tt: This container no longer exists on the host. Edit the group to remove it.
web_groups_drag_tt: Drag to reorder. The first one is the head.
web_groups_no_members: No containers in this group yet.
web_groups_autodetect_intro: Each card is a detected stack (containers grouped by `com.docker.compose.project` or `com.docker.stack.namespace`). Check the ones you want to import as Docksentry groups. Drag rows inside a card to set the head order before importing.
web_groups_autodetect_none: No Compose / Portainer / Swarm stacks detected on this host. Stacks need the standard project labels — manual `docker run` containers can't be auto-detected.
web_groups_autodetect_conflict: ⚠ Already in group `{group}` — will be moved on import.
web_groups_autodetect_skip_existing: Stack already imported (group exists with same name)
data_loss_alert:
⚠️ *No persisted settings found* — possible data loss.

Your Telegram config came from env vars, but `/data/settings.json` is missing. Container groups, pin / autoupdate / link / window state may have been lost too. Common causes: host reboot mid-write (fixed in v1.22.0 with atomic writes — won't happen again), volume mount missing at start, fresh `/data/` volume.

If you have a backup, restore via Web UI → Settings → Import. Otherwise re-configure and check the Web UI's Status page for any groups / pins you'd set up.
storage_wrong_mount:
⚠️ *Your data directory is not where you think it is*

`{source}` is mounted at `{dest}`, but Docksentry never reads or writes there — its data lives in `{data_dir}`. So that directory stays empty, and everything Docksentry saves goes to an anonymous volume that is thrown away the next time this container is recreated: by `compose down`/`up`, by a `docker rm`, or by a self-update.

Fix the mount and the losses stop:

`- {source}:{data_dir}`

Restore your last backup afterwards (Web UI → Settings → Import) — this time it will stay.
storage_anonymous:
⚠️ *Nothing here survives a recreate*

`{data_dir}` is an anonymous volume — Docker made one because nothing was mounted there. It is a fresh one for every container, so settings, groups and pins are discarded the next time this container is recreated: by `compose down`/`up`, by a `docker rm`, or by a self-update.

Mount a directory or a named volume at `{data_dir}`, for example:

`- ./docksentry-data:{data_dir}`
storage_unmounted:
⚠️ *Nothing here survives a recreate*

Nothing is mounted at `{data_dir}`, so everything saved there lives inside the container itself and goes when the container goes — on `compose down`/`up`, on a `docker rm`, or on a self-update.

Mount a directory or a named volume at `{data_dir}`, for example:

`- ./docksentry-data:{data_dir}`
web_backup_intro: Export every persisted setting (groups, notes, links, pins, autoupdate flags, update windows, webhook URLs, etc.) into a single JSON file. Restore it later — useful before host migrations, or just as defense-in-depth against data loss.
web_backup_hint: Backups contain webhook URLs and bot tokens — treat the file like a password. The import path skips unknown keys, so forward-compatible if a future Docksentry adds new settings.
update_snapshot_stale_msg: ⚠️ That "Updates Available" notification is too old to act on (a newer check has replaced it, or the bot restarted). Run /check for a fresh list.
selfupdate_old_tag:
✅ The `:{current}` image tag is up to date — but that's a *fixed version*, and a newer release (`v{latest}`) exists. Your container won't move past `:{current}` on its own. To upgrade:
• `/selfupdate {latest}` (jump to the new version), or
• `/selfupdate latest` (rejoin the rolling latest line), or
• set `image: amayer1983/docksentry:latest` in your compose and `docker compose up -d`.
policy_held: ⏸ `{name}`: held back by update policy ({level} {old} → {new}). Run /update {name} to apply, or set docksentry.policy=all.
age_held: ⏳ *{name}*: actualización retenida — la nueva imagen tiene {days} día(s) y este contenedor espera {required}. Se aplicará automáticamente en unos {remaining} día(s).
web_check_one_tt: Buscar ahora actualizaciones para este contenedor
web_check_one_busy: Ahora mismo hay una actualización en curso: inténtalo de nuevo en un momento
web_selfupdate_marker_tt: Docksentry se actualiza mediante AUTO_SELFUPDATE, no mediante la lista de auto-actualización por contenedor — se cambia en Configuración › Updates.
web_selfupdate_settings_tt: La auto-actualización propia se ajusta en Configuración › Updates — abre esa página.
web_detail_selfupdate_hint: Docksentry se actualiza únicamente mediante AUTO_SELFUPDATE; la lista de auto-actualización por contenedor no se le aplica. El interruptor está en Configuración › Updates.
web_update_tt: Descargar la nueva imagen y recrear este contenedor — se conservan volúmenes, puertos, red y variables de entorno.
web_pin_tt: Fijar a la imagen actual — las comprobaciones de actualización omiten este contenedor hasta que lo desfijes.
web_unpin_tt: Quitar la fijación — este contenedor vuelve a participar en las comprobaciones de actualización.
web_restart_tt: Reiniciar este contenedor — misma imagen, misma configuración, solo una breve interrupción.
web_stop_tt: Detener este contenedor — permanecerá apagado hasta que alguien lo inicie de nuevo; los datos y la configuración se conservan.
web_link_open_tt: Abrir la página de repositorio / changelog de este contenedor en una pestaña nueva
web_link_origin_label: de la etiqueta de contenedor docksentry.link
web_link_origin_source: de la etiqueta de imagen org.opencontainers.image.source
web_link_origin_url: de la etiqueta de imagen org.opencontainers.image.url
web_link_origin_registry: deducido del nombre de la imagen — página general del registro, no un changelog
web_link_cleared: Enlace eliminado — vuelve a aplicarse la detección automática.
web_link_rejected: Enlace rechazado: solo se aceptan URLs completas http:// o https://, sin espacios ni comillas.
web_healthcheck_max_starting_hint: Tiempo máximo que un contenedor actualizado tiene para informar como «healthy» antes de que la actualización se considere fallida y se revierta.
web_docker_stop_timeout_hint: Cuánto espera «docker stop» a que un contenedor se detenga por sí solo antes de forzar su cierre.
web_monitor_enabled: Monitorizar el estado de los contenedores
web_monitor_hint: Vigila los contenedores en ejecución y envía una alerta cuando uno se detiene, muere o pasa a estado unhealthy.
web_monitor_interval_hint: Con qué frecuencia se consulta el estado de los contenedores. Mínimo 15 segundos.
web_password_hint: Contraseña para la autenticación HTTP básica de esta interfaz. Déjalo vacío para mantener la actual; una nueva contraseña se aplica de inmediato.
host_local_only_hint: ℹ️ Local host only — add `@<host>` or `@all` for the others.
help_hosts: /hosts — Show the hosts this instance manages
web_audit_intro: State-changing actions from the Web UI, Telegram, Discord and the scheduler. Secrets are never recorded.
monitor_oom_flag_yes: ⚠️ The kernel OOM-killed it — this was memory.
monitor_oom_flag_no: Not an OOM kill — the exit code came from something else.
startup_hard_kill: ⚠️ The previous run was killed rather than stopped — no clean shutdown was recorded. Exit 137 usually means the kernel or the runtime ended it: check host memory and CPU load around that time.
recovery_restored: 🔧 An update was interrupted mid-swap. {name} was left stopped under a backup name and has been restored and started.
recovery_stale: 🔧 An update to {name} was interrupted more than a day ago and `{old}` is still there. Not touched — too old to act on safely.
recovery_failed: ⚠️ An update to {name} was interrupted and `{old}` could not be restored automatically. It needs a hand.
recovery_gone: ⚠️ An update to {name} was interrupted and neither the container nor its backup is there any more.
web_badge_newer_tt: Pinned to {current}. Version {newer} exists on the registry — Docksentry will not switch to it, because the tag you pinned is what it keeps running. Change the tag in your compose file to move.
web_discord_bot_intro: Opcional, e independiente del webhook de arriba. Un token de bot permite que Docksentry reciba comandos en Discord — /status, /update, /logs y 19 más — en vez de solo enviar notificaciones. Crea la aplicación en discord.com/developers/applications.
web_discord_token_help: De la página Bot de tu aplicación de Discord. Se guarda en settings.json, legible solo por su propietario. Déjalo vacío para conservar el token guardado.
web_discord_token_clear_help: Borra el token y detiene el bot. El webhook de Discord de arriba no se ve afectado.
web_discord_app_id_help: De General Information en tu aplicación de Discord. Obligatorio — los comandos de barra se registran contra él.
web_discord_guild_id_help: El servidor de Discord al que se limita el bot. Obligatorio. Activa el modo desarrollador en Discord, haz clic derecho en el nombre del servidor y elige Copiar ID del servidor.
web_discord_allowed_users: IDs de usuario de Discord permitidos
web_discord_allowed_users_help: Opcional — IDs de usuario de Discord separados por comas que pueden ejecutar comandos. Déjalo vacío para permitir a cualquiera del servidor de arriba.
web_discord_bot_started: Bot de Discord reiniciado y conectado.
web_discord_bot_off: El bot de Discord está apagado — necesita token de bot e ID de aplicación.
web_discord_bot_no_guild: Guardado, pero el bot no arrancó: falta el ID del servidor. Es lo que limita el bot a tu servidor.
web_discord_bot_bad_token: Guardado, pero Discord rechazó el token.
web_discord_bot_no_commands: Bot conectado, pero falló el registro de los comandos de barra. Pueden tardar en aparecer.
web_discord_bot_error: Guardado, pero no se pudo iniciar el bot.
web_connections_intro: A dónde envía Docksentry sus notificaciones y cuáles pueden devolver comandos. Los ajustes deciden cuándo actúa Docksentry; esta página decide dónde habla.
web_conn_telegram_intro: El token del bot y el ID de chat se definen como variables de entorno. Lo de aquí se aplica al bot que ya está en marcha.
web_conn_webhooks_intro: Notificaciones en un solo sentido. Discord admite incrustaciones enriquecidas; el webhook genérico envía JSON a cualquier cosa que lo acepte.
web_conn_smtp_intro: Notificaciones por correo. Activo en cuanto servidor, remitente y destinatario están puestos.
web_smtp_host_help: Nombre o dirección del servidor SMTP.
web_smtp_port_help: 587 para STARTTLS, 465 para SSL, 25 para un relé sin cifrar.
web_smtp_tls_help: STARTTLS mejora una conexión en claro; SSL va cifrado desde el primer byte. «Ninguno» envía todo en claro y solo vale para un relé en tu propia máquina.
web_smtp_from_help: La dirección del remitente. Algunos proveedores rechazan cualquier cosa que no sea la dirección de la cuenta.
web_smtp_user_help: Déjalo vacío para un relé que no autentica.
web_smtp_password_help: Se guarda en settings.json, legible solo por su propietario. Déjalo vacío para conservar la contraseña guardada.
web_smtp_password_clear_help: Borra la contraseña. El resto de los ajustes de correo se mantienen.
web_smtp_tls_verify_help: Déjalo activado. Desactivado, la contraseña se envía a lo que responda en esa dirección, con cualquier certificado — desactívalo solo para un servidor interno con certificado autofirmado, y quedará dicho en el registro cada vez que se use.
web_conn_ntfy_intro: Notificaciones push al móvil o al escritorio mediante ntfy. O una URL de tema completa, o un servidor y un tema.
web_ntfy_url_help: Todo junto, p. ej. https://ntfy.sh/mi-tema. Pon esto O los dos campos de abajo, no ambos.
web_ntfy_server_help: Solo el servidor, p. ej. https://ntfy.sh — junto con el tema de abajo.
web_ntfy_topic_help: El nombre del tema en ese servidor. Quien lo conozca lee tus notificaciones: elige algo impredecible.
web_ntfy_token_help: Para un tema protegido. Como alternativa, usa el usuario y la contraseña de abajo.
web_ntfy_user_help: Solo para un tema protegido con usuario y contraseña en vez de con un token.
web_ntfy_password_help: Se guarda en settings.json, legible solo por su propietario.
web_conn_gotify_intro: Un servidor push autoalojado. Necesita la dirección del servidor y un token de aplicación.
web_gotify_url_help: El servidor Gotify, p. ej. https://gotify.example.com. La ruta /message se añade si falta.
web_gotify_token_help: Desde Apps en tu servidor Gotify — un token de aplicación, no uno de cliente.
web_conn_matrix_intro: Notificaciones en una sala de Matrix.
web_matrix_homeserver_help: p. ej. https://matrix.org, o el tuyo propio.
web_matrix_room_help: ID o alias de la sala, p. ej. #docksentry:matrix.org.
web_matrix_token_help: El token de la cuenta que publica. En Element: Ajustes → Ayuda y acerca de → Token de acceso.
web_conn_apprise_intro: Un servidor de API Apprise, que reenvía a más de cien servicios. Úsalo cuando el canal que quieres no esté arriba.
web_apprise_url_help: Tu servidor de API Apprise, p. ej. http://apprise:8000/notify.
web_apprise_urls_help: Las URL de destino de Apprise, separadas por comas. Suelen contener credenciales, así que se tratan como secreto y nunca se muestran de vuelta.
web_apprise_tag_help: Opcional — notificar solo a los destinos que lleven esta etiqueta.
web_conn_discord_hook_intro: Avisos de actualización como incrustaciones en un canal de Discord. Independiente del bot de abajo, que recibe comandos.
web_conn_webhook_intro: Envía JSON a cualquier cosa que lo acepte: tu propio script, una plataforma de automatización, lo que tengas.
web_chan_none_body: Docksentry seguirá comprobando y actualizando, pero no tendrá forma de contártelo: solo esta interfaz web.
web_leftover_title: Copias de seguridad de actualización sobrantes
web_leftover_intro: {count} contenedor(es) llamados <nombre>_old quedaron de una actualización interrumpida. Son copias detenidas de contenedores que se actualizaron bien: se pueden borrar sin riesgo, y aquí nadie los borra por ti.
web_badge_podman_auto_tt: Este contenedor lleva io.containers.autoupdate={mode}, así que `podman auto-update` también lo gestiona. Dos actualizadores sobre un contenedor: gana el que se ejecute primero. Docksentry lo sigue actualizando si se lo pides, pero conviene saber que no está solo.
web_host_contexts: Docker conoce estos extremos en esta máquina: {list} — útil si la dirección de arriba tiene una errata.
web_discord_bot_channel_help: Donde el bot escribe por su cuenta: arranque, alertas, resultados de actualización. Permanente y visible para todo el canal, a diferencia de las respuestas a comandos. Activa el modo desarrollador, clic derecho en el canal, Copiar ID del canal.
web_discord_public_replies: Respuestas a comandos visibles para todos
web_discord_public_replies_help: Desactivado, solo quien lanzó el comando ve la respuesta y luego se borra sola. Activado, permanece en el canal para todos. Desactivado por defecto: una lista de contenedores nombra tus servicios internos.
web_conn_discordbot_intro: El bot hablando por su cuenta, en vez de solo responder. Necesita el token del bot de arriba y un ID de canal.
web_discord_dup_title: Los avisos de Discord llegarán dos veces
web_discord_dup_intro: El webhook de Discord y el canal del bot están ambos activos, así que cada aviso lo publica cada uno. Está permitido —quizá quieras uno público y otro privado— pero si no era la intención, desactiva uno.
web_api_tokens_intro: Acceso de solo lectura a /metrics y GET /api/status sin la contraseña de la interfaz web. Solo se define mediante la variable de entorno API_TOKENS; aquí nunca se muestran los tokens, solo sus nombres.
web_api_tokens_none: No hay tokens configurados. Ambos extremos exigen entonces la contraseña de la interfaz web, que un recolector no puede proporcionar.
web_api_tokens_hint: El uso se cuenta en memoria, así que un reinicio lo borra: «no desde el último reinicio» no significa que el token esté sin usar.
web_api_tokens_broken: no hay token tras los dos puntos: esta entrada nunca podrá coincidir
web_api_tokens_overruled: API_TOKENS está definida en el entorno, pero un valor guardado tiene prioridad sobre ella: vale lo que aparece aquí. Borra el valor guardado para que la variable surta efecto.
web_username_help: Opcional. Si se deja vacío se acepta cualquier usuario, como hacía Docksentry cuando no existía ninguno. Si lo defines, solo se acepta ese nombre.
web_session_hours: La sesión caduca por inactividad tras (horas)
web_session_hours_help: Cuánto sobrevive una sesión del navegador sin usarse. Basta con volver a iniciar sesión.
web_session_max_days: La sesión caduca como máximo tras (días)
web_session_max_days_help: Pasado ese tiempo la sesión termina en cualquier caso, incluso una que una pestaña en segundo plano mantenga viva.
web_password_hashed: Se guarda como hash y no se puede volver a mostrar.
web_setup_pw_intro: Establece una contraseña para que solo tú accedas al panel. Se guarda como hash, nunca en texto plano, y puedes cambiarla después en Ajustes.
web_setup_pw_none: Funcionar sin contraseña: solo detrás de un proxy inverso o en una red de confianza
web_setup_pw_required: Elige una contraseña o marca la casilla para funcionar sin ella.
update_queued: 🕒 `{name}` en cola — posición {pos}. Empieza cuando termine la actualización actual.
update_queue_full: ⚠️ La cola está llena ({max}). Espera a que se vacíe y vuelve a tocar.
update_queue_dropped_selfupdate: ⚠️ Hay una autoactualización pendiente, Docksentry va a reiniciarse. NO se ejecutaron: {names}. Vuelve a tocarlos después.
update_queue_skipped_group: ⚠️ Se omitió el resto del grupo `{group}` tras el fallo anterior: {names}. Se actualizan en orden por una razón — arregla primero el que falló.
web_hidden_active_title: Active settings you cannot see here
web_hidden_active_intro: Simple mode hides the advanced options, and {count} of them are not at their default — so they are doing something on this instance while being off the page. Switch to advanced to see and change them.
web_env_card_intro: These are set in your environment, but a value saved here wins. That is deliberate — otherwise anything you change in this interface would be reset on the next restart. Take the environment's value back whenever you would rather have it.
help_backup: /backup — Send a backup of settings, groups and pins as a file
help_detail_backup:
*/backup*

Builds the same bundle the Web UI exports — persisted settings, container groups, pins, auto-update flags, notes, links and update windows — and sends it into this chat as a file.

A copy is written to `/data/backups/` at the same time, and the five most recent are kept.

_The file contains your saved settings, which includes webhook URLs and the Web UI password hash. It goes to this chat only, but treat it the way you would treat the file itself._
backup_caption: 📦 Docksentry backup — restore via Web UI → Settings → Import.
backup_send_failed: ⚠️ The backup was built but Telegram would not take the file. Try again, or download it from the Web UI under Settings.
web_setup_restore_intro: Already have a backup from another install, or from this one? Restore it and skip the rest of this.
web_status_view_hint: How your containers are drawn. The table shows every action on every row and suits a wide screen. The list shows one row per container leading with whether an update is waiting, puts the rest in a detail panel, and reads on a phone.
web_status_view_list: List — update state first, details on demand
restore_expired: ⚠️ That offer is gone — send the file again.
restore_too_big: ⚠️ {size} MB is too large for a backup file. Nothing was downloaded.
restore_download_failed: ⚠️ Telegram would not hand me that file.
restore_not_json: ⚠️ That file is not JSON, so it is not a Docksentry backup.
restore_not_a_backup: ⚠️ That is JSON, but not a Docksentry backup — no `schema_version` in it.
restart_going_down: 🔄 Restarting — back in a moment. (restart policy: `{policy}`)
startup_reason_requested: ↻ _Restarted on request — the restart button or `/restart`._
help_detail_restart:
*/restart*

Stops Docksentry so its container's restart policy brings it back — which is how settings that only apply at boot take effect.

It checks that policy first. Without one, stopping would leave the container down and you without the bot you would use to bring it back, so it refuses and says so instead.

The next start knows it was asked for, rather than reporting an external stop signal.
host_check_recovered: ✅ Host `{host}` is reachable again — it is back in the scheduled check.
hosts_single: This instance manages a single host.
restore_how:
📥 *Restoring*

Send the backup file into this chat — drag it in, or forward one from another Docksentry's chat. I will say what it contains and ask before changing anything.

Use `/backup` to get one.
help_restore: /restore — Restore from a backup file sent into this chat
help_detail_restore:
*/restore*

Send a Docksentry backup into this chat and I will offer to restore it. Dragging the file in is enough — the command itself only explains how.

Before anything changes you get told which instance the bundle came from, when it was made and what it would overwrite. The button is the decision, not the file arriving.

Unknown settings are dropped and links are checked, because a backup is a file and nothing about you picking it says you wrote it.
help_detail_hosts:
*/hosts*

Lists every host this instance manages and the endpoint it reaches each one through. On a single-host install it says so.

Useful when a check reports a host as unreachable: the endpoint here is the one that failed.
help_updateall: /updateall — Update every container with a pending update
help_detail_updateall:
*/updateall*

Updates everything currently listed as having an update, exactly like the *Update all* button under an update notification.

Pinned containers are skipped, groups are updated in order, and a failure stops that group but not the others.
note_usage: Usage: `/note <container> <text>` — leave the text off to clear it.
trust_empty: 🩺 Nothing is set to accept running-but-unhealthy.
trust_on: ✅ `{name}`: a running-but-unhealthy result will be accepted after an update.
trust_off: ⬜ `{name}`: health has to come back green again.
askmajor_list: ⚠️ Ask before a major update for:
askmajor_empty: ⚠️ No container asks before a major update.
askmajor_on: ✅ `{name}`: a major version jump will ask first.
askmajor_off: ⬜ `{name}`: major updates apply like any other.
testchannel_sending: 🔔 Sending a test to every channel that is switched on…
testchannel_message: 🔔 Test notification — if you can read this on a channel, that channel works.
help_note: /note — Attach a note to a container
help_detail_note:
*/note <container> [text]*

Attaches a short note to a container, shown next to it in the Web UI. Leave the text off to clear it.

For the things you will not remember in three months: why this one is pinned, which compose file it comes from, who else depends on it.
help_detail_trustrunning:
*/trustrunning <container>*

Some containers never report healthy — no healthcheck, or one that only passes under load. After an update Docksentry waits for health and rolls back when it does not come; for these, running is as good as it gets.

With this set, a container that is up but not green counts as a successful update. Without an argument it lists what is set.

Use it sparingly: it switches off the check that catches an update which started and then broke.
help_askmajor: /askmajor — Ask before applying a major update
help_detail_askmajor:
*/askmajor <container>*

A major version jump — 16 → 17 on a database, say — asks before it is applied rather than going ahead. You get the question with the update, and nothing happens until you answer.

Without an argument it lists what is set.
help_testchannel: /testchannel — Send a test notification to every channel
help_detail_testchannel:
*/testchannel*

Sends one message through every notification channel that is switched on — Telegram, Discord, e-mail, ntfy, Gotify, Matrix, Apprise, webhook.

More useful from here than from the Web UI: you are already standing where the message has to arrive, so "did it work?" answers itself. A channel that stays quiet is a channel to look at.
startup_killed_stopping: ⚠️ _The previous run was killed before it finished shutting down — `docker stop` ran out of patience and sent SIGKILL (exit 137). Nothing should be lost, every file is written atomically, but a longer `DOCKER_STOP_TIMEOUT` gives the web server, the scheduler and the Discord gateway time to come to a stop._
web_label_card_intro: Prefixed to every message on every channel — Telegram, Discord, e-mail, ntfy, Gotify, Matrix, Apprise and webhooks alike. Set it when more than one Docksentry reports into the same place, so you can tell which machine is talking.
audit_section_dropped: *Skipped on purpose* — set on this container, known to us, and not carried on recreate:
chan_testchannel_sent: 🔔 Enviado a todos los canales activados.
chan_no_backend: No hay backend de contenedores disponible.
chan_confirm_not_yours: Solo quien ejecutó el comando puede confirmarlo.
chan_maint_off: 🔧 El modo de mantenimiento está **desactivado**: las actualizaciones siguen su horario.
chan_maint_on: 🔧 El modo de mantenimiento está **activado** hasta que lo desactives.
chan_maint_on_until: 🔧 El modo de mantenimiento está **activado** hasta {until}.
chan_maint_remaining: 🔧 El modo de mantenimiento está **activado**: quedan {remaining}.
chan_restore_restart_hint: Algunos ajustes solo se aplican tras reiniciar: `/restart` sin contenedor lo hace.
chan_bad_duration: No se pudo leer `{value}` como duración. Prueba `2h`, `30m`, `1d`, `forever` u `off`.
chan_backup_upload_failed: ⚠️ La copia se creó, pero el chat no aceptó el archivo. Descárgala desde la interfaz web.
chan_file_too_large: ⚠️ {size} MB es demasiado para un archivo de copia. No se descargó nada.
chan_attachment_http: ⚠️ El chat no me entregó ese archivo: respondió **HTTP {code}**. Intenta adjuntarlo de nuevo.
chan_selfupdate_started: ⬆️ Autoactualización iniciada: avisaré en el canal cuando termine y reiniciaré si hay algo que aplicar.
chan_nothing_left: No queda nada por actualizar: todos los contenedores aprobados ya están actualizados.
chan_debug_toggled: 🔍 Registro de depuración **{status}**. Muestra cada llamada al registro y el detalle por contenedor de un escaneo.
major_none_pending: ⚠️ No hay actualización mayor pendiente para `{name}`.
window_skipped: ⏰ Fuera de la ventana de mantenimiento: actualización automática omitida para {names}
restart_no_own_name: No puedo saber qué contenedor soy.
restart_no_policy_reported: el demonio no informó una política de reinicio.
restart_policy_is_none: la política de reinicio de este contenedor es `{policy}`.
selfupdate_helper_pull_failed: ❌ Falló la autoactualización: no se pudo descargar la imagen auxiliar `docker:cli` — {error}
groups_empty: No hay grupos de contenedores configurados.
link_unsafe: ⚠️ `{url}` no es un enlace seguro: solo http(s).
chan_autocleanup_on: La limpieza automática está **activada**: ocurre sola.
logs_failed: No se pudieron leer los registros de `{name}`: {error}
chan_no_backend_for: No hay backend de contenedores para `{name}`.
lifecycle_refused_busy: Hay una actualización en curso: `{action}` se rechaza hasta que termine.
chan_busy_capacity: ⏳ Docksentry ya ejecuta tantos comandos como puede a la vez. **No se inició nada.** Inténtalo en un momento.
chan_working_on_it:
⏳ Trabajando en ello: puede tardar unos minutos.
Si supera la ventana de respuesta de Discord, publicaré el resultado en el canal.
chan_late_result: (esto superó la ventana de respuesta, así que aquí está el resultado como mensaje normal)
chan_confirm_expired: Esa confirmación caducó o ya se usó: ejecuta el comando de nuevo si aún lo quieres.
chan_update_busy: ⏳ Ya hay una actualización en curso: no se inició nada. Inténtalo cuando termine.
chan_list_failed: No se pudieron listar los contenedores: {error}
chan_backup_caption: 📦 Copia de Docksentry: restaura desde la interfaz web → Ajustes → Importar.
chan_restore_warning: Restaurar sobrescribe los ajustes, grupos, pines, notas, enlaces y ventanas de actualización de **esta** instancia.
chan_confirm_stop: ⚠ ¿Detener `{name}`? Seguirá parado hasta que algo lo inicie de nuevo.
chan_updateall_confirm: Cada uno se descarga y se recrea. Pulsa el botón para continuar.
chan_skipped_not_pending: ℹ {count} de los {total} contenedores aprobados ya no estaban pendientes y se omitieron.
chan_newly_pending: ℹ Aparecieron {count} contenedores pendientes tras preguntarte y NO se actualizaron: ejecuta `/updateall` de nuevo.
chat_migrated: ⚠️ Este grupo pasó a supergrupo, así que el `CHAT_ID={old}` configurado ya no existe. Encontré el nuevo y lo estoy usando: `{new}`. Ponlo en tus ajustes — hasta entonces tengo que redescubrirlo tras cada reinicio.
